items.title: An alpha-universal class contains every structure whose Scott sentence is in the Pi-alpha class
items.author: David Gonzalez; Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 795-798: if a class K_0 is alpha-universal for a class K_1, then K_0 contains every structure of K_1 that has a P_infinity alpha Scott sentence. The proof (source lines 799-804) is short but it is not a formality: it has to pick a counterexample, obtain a comparison partner from the universality hypothesis, and then convert that comparison into an isomorphism by the defining property of a Scott sentence of that class, which is what puts the structure back into K_0. The statement records only the containment and hides that the whole content is the interaction between the universality relation and the isomorphism characterisation supplied by the Scott sentence.
